description: §55.8 / §55.10 / §41.12.1 — a resolved error message is TEXT at every `` sink. A cross-field payload is user data: `eq(@signup.password)` puts whatever was typed into the password field into `{expected}`, and `neq(@signup.password)` into `{forbidden}`. Typing `` into the password field must not create an element — not through a registered (Level 2) template, not through the shipped (Level 3) default, not in the per-field render, not in the compound `all` rollup — and author text in a template (`{field}`) renders literally, exactly as the same message does through a `${ messageFor(...) }` text interpolation.
rationale:
§55.8 normative default rendering is `

${ messageFor(errors[0]) }

` — a markup `${}` text interpolation, so the message is text and the default render must produce the same DOM a text interpolation does. Pre-fix (S462 FIX ROUND 1 P1, pre-existing since C11) the default render concatenated the message into an HTML string assigned to innerHTML, so a user-typed payload became markup (an `#pwn` element was created). The `#e-text` paragraph is the control: the same message through an ordinary `${}` interpolation. The Level-3 default wording is impl-freedom, so the `#e-hint` assertions are structural (one error paragraph, no element inside it).
